chief_complaint: unbearable nocturnal itching and finger web burrows
hpi_details: A 62-year-old female presents to the clinic with unbearable nocturnal itching and finger web burrows. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: thinks it might be related to scabies
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Scabies is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Scabies: Topical Permethrin 5% cream full body (repeat in 7 days), treat family, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Scabies.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Eczema without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Widespread crusted, hyperkeratotic lesions with minimal itch in an elderly or immunocompromised patient — think crusted (Norwegian) scabies, which is highly contagious.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Scabies
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Scabies
Implement evidence-based management plan: Topical Permethrin 5% cream full body (repeat in 7 days), treat family

teaching.one_liner: A mite infestation causing intense nocturnal itching with burrows in the finger webs.
red_flags: Widespread crusted, hyperkeratotic lesions with minimal itch in an elderly or immunocompromised patient — think crusted (Norwegian) scabies, which is highly contagious
Signs of secondary bacterial infection (cellulitis, impetiginization) — risk of post-streptococcal complications
Outbreak among household or close contacts — all contacts need simultaneous treatment

must_ask.say: Is the itching worse at night?
Where is the itching worst — between your fingers?
Has anyone around you had similar itching?
How long has this been going on?
Have you seen any thin lines on your skin?
